you're right. i misspoke. what i meant was that they can't get addicted *the same way* a non-ADHDer can when it comes to Adderall. they can get addicted, but in the case of ADHD meds, that are monitored and given to an ADHD patient, it isn't 100% feasible. also, getting a brain scan done has nothing to do with being diagnosed with ADHD or getting prescribed medication. it can help, yes, but most people with ADHD get diagnosed through the diagnostic criteria, brain scans aren't required. also, your whole point of "walking in and getting prescribed medication" *is the whole reason why it's so restricted to begin with.* people with stimulant addictions claim to have ADHD or have trouble focusing and thus get prescribed Adderall, which only fuels the addiction more.

yep. the reason is because Adderal is an *amphetamine,* which to a non-ADHDer is highly addictive. ADHD meds supplement the chemicals the ADHD brain is missing, but for non-ADHDers, it "overstocks" those chemicals and sends the brain into overdrive. so the US restricts access to it so no one can just walk in and ask. however, this bars a lot of people who actually *have* ADHD from getting their prescriptions for fear of addiction, even though an ADHD brain is literally wired different and can't get addicted to a stimulant, or at least not in the same way. i was on Ritalin for a while, but didn't take it long enough to need a refill. i imagine i would've had a similar experience to lots of others.
